subject: EU-only inference: operator access & retention exceptions
messages:

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 07:58:00 +0200
Subject: EU-only inference — operator access & retention clarifications

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we continue our security review at NovusHealth, a couple of operational questions came up around your "EU-only inference" option that I wanted to confirm before we move to legal/procurement:

1) Operator access exceptions: We need a clear description of who (Redwood employees, sub-processors) can ever access plaintext request/response data while a tenant is on the EU-only plan. Specifically — are there documented emergency or legal-access exceptions that could result in data being processed outside the EU?

2) Backups and disaster recovery: Does your backup/restore process create copies outside the EU and what is your deletion/retention guarantee for backups when a customer requests deletion?

3) SCCs / Schrems II implications: If you route control-plane signals to non-EU regions (e.g., for telemetry), can you confirm whether SCCs are in place and whether you provide attestation of operational controls?

Can you send an operational note or runbook fragment that we can share with our privacy team? Also include any artifacts you can provide (SCCs, SOC2 pages, runbook snippets).

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Data Protection Officer | NovusHealth

Subject: Re: EU-only inference — operator access & retention clarifications

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I've looped in Naomi (privacy) and Irene (ops) to provide the technical and control detail you requested. High level answers below; Naomi will follow with specifics and artifacts.

Summary (short):
- Operator access: By default, no Redwood engineer has plaintext access to customer inference payloads in EU-only deployments. There are two narrow exceptions: (a) customer-authorized troubleshooting session (explicit, time-limited access with audit), and (b) legal/compelled access where we will notify customers unless prohibited. Any such access is logged and subject to SCCs and our internal access review process.
- Backups/DR: Backups for EU-only tenants are stored in EU regions only. Snapshot retention default is 30 days; retention can be shortened or set to immediate purge at contract setup. We provide deletion evidence for backups (snapshot id + timestamp).
- SCCs & telemetry: SCCs are executed for cross-border transfers. Control-plane telemetry that leaves the EU is minimized; where it does occur we have contractual SCCs in place and a documented pseudonymization layer.

I'll attach a short runbook draft for ops and propose a short sync to walk through the artifacts. Proposed next steps:
1) Naomi to send SCCs mapping + sample attestation.
2) Irene to attach runbook snippet for emergency access and backup deletion flow.
3) We schedule a 30-min call for Tuesday/Wednesday next week.

Attachments: EU-only-runbook-draft.pdf (runbook fragment)

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the questions. I wanted to provide the detailed Q&A and point you to the artifacts we can share immediately. Below are concise answers followed by what we can deliver today.

Operator access (details):
- Default state: No human has routine access to customer inference payloads in EU-only deployments. The runtime is deployed into customer VPCs or dedicated EU clusters where access controls are enforced via RBAC and Identity-Aware Proxy.
- Exceptional access paths:
  * Customer-authorized troubleshooting: we require a written request (email + ticket) from an authorized customer admin. Access is time-boxed (max 48 hours), recorded, and scoped to the minimum required resources.
  * Legal compulsion: if compelled by lawful process, we comply per SCCs and local law; we notify the customer unless prohibited.
  * Emergency safety-of-life: approved by our Incident Response lead + legal; fully audited.
- Operators are prevented from exfiltrating plaintext by logging controls, limited shell access, and mandatory session recording for any elevated sessions.

Backups & retention (details):
- All snapshots and backups for EU-only tenants are provisioned in EU regions (we use GCP EU and AWS eu-west equivalents depending on the deployment). No backups are replicated outside the EU by default.
- Retention: default 30-day snapshots; customer can request 0-day retention at provisioning or a contractual retention window.
- Deletion evidence: when a deletion request is processed we provide a signed deletion record (snapshot ids, deletion timestamps, and runbook step id).

SCCs & Schrems II:
- We execute the standard EU Commission SCCs for data transfers where required and maintain mappings between processing activities and SCC clauses.
- For telemetry/control-plane signals that are pseudonymized and aggregated, we apply an operator-controlled pseudonymization layer and minimize identifiers. We can provide an SCC appendix that documents which control-plane endpoints are covered.

Artifacts we can share today:
- Draft "EU-only runbook fragment" (attached) — shows emergency access steps, approval flow, and audit sample.
- SCCs mapping spreadsheet (we'll provide a redlined sample) — attestation available under NDA.
- SOC2 summary page (non-sensitive) and pointer to our compliance pack.

Follow-ups / ask from NovusHealth:
- Can you confirm the backup retention window you want in contract? (default 30 days vs 0/contracted)
- Would NovusHealth like an on-site or live walk-through of the runbook and the audit logs?

Next: Irene will add a short operational appendix on how we produce deletion evidence (cron job, retention TTL, verification).

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Trust, Redwood Inference
